findings.quote: I used the same equation for both stages
findings.note: It never names the equation, so it reads close to a generic 'I used the formula' while the three wrong routes all name a concrete quantity; a student scanning the menu has to guess which equation is meant. The 'both stages' half is the correct separator and should be kept.
findings.fix: I used v²=u²−2as for each stage

notes: Right route is deliberately not step 1 and that is correct here: step 1 (v = 2u/3) is shared by the option-1 and option-4 wrong routes, so under the separation rule the earliest unshared step is applying v²=u²−2as to each stage. All three types are application by the definition (the concept is known but is attached to the wrong quantity, a speed fraction instead of a distance ratio); concept is arguable for all three, but this is a boundary I did not file. Each route matches its own entry and indices 0/1/2 align. I checked mistakes[0] 'the speed left' against mistakes[1] 'the speed lost' as a possible cannot-tell-apart pair and did not file it: the student knows whether they wrote 2/3 or 1/3, and left/lost is a one-word difference a Class-11 student reads correctly - but it is the thinnest pair in this slice. No route names a two-digit number or an option value (2/3, 1/3, 4/9, 4/5 all absent).
